rci8_quality_checking.detail: Manual visual inspection by three trained raters using T1 QA scoring (unusable/decent/superior); automated T1 SNR estimation; 47 individuals excluded due to unusable imaging data (3.7%); T1 QA and T1 SNR tested as potential covariates in sensitivity analyses
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: All T1-weighted images underwent rigorous quality control by three highly trained image analysts. Briefly, all images were visually inspected and evaluated for the presence of artifacts. Images with gross artifacts were considered unusable; images with some artifacts were flagged as 'decent'; and images free of artifact were marked as 'superior'. Ratings of scan quality were averaged over the three raters and we hereafter refer to this average measure as T1 quality assurance (T1 QA). As mentioned above in the section titled Participants, 47 individuals were removed due to unusable imaging data according to this T1 QA measure. As a result, 1,054 (83%) of our 1,271 participants had T1-weighted images identified as 'superior', with the remaining identified as 'usable'. In addition to the above rater-based estimate of T1-weighted image quality, we also estimated the signal-to-noise ratio of each participant's T1-weighted image (T1 SNR).

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Ridge regression (α=1) with 100 repeats of 10-fold cross-validation to predict psychopathology dimensions from multivariate patterns of deviations; PCA dimensionality reduction to 9 PCs; scoring metrics: RMSE, MAE, and correlation between true and predicted values; permutation testing (100,000 permutations) for significance; exact test of differences to compare deviations vs. raw volume; Pearson correlations between regional deviations and psychopathology dimensions; bootstrapped comparisons (10,000 samples) of effect sizes between overall psychopathology and specific dimensions; mass univariate analysis across 400 Schaefer parcels with FDR correction (q=0.05); case-control comparisons using Cohen's d for depression and ADHD groups vs. matched healthy controls; spatial Pearson correlation between regional Cohen's d values for depression and ADHD groups; sensitivity analyses controlling for maternal education, T1 QA, T1 SNR, and general intelligence (WRAT-4)
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Multivariate patterns of cortical volume deviations from normative models improved out-of-sample prediction of overall psychopathology, psychosis-positive symptoms, and fear compared to raw cortical volume; overall psychopathology showed stronger correlations with deviations in vmPFC, inferior temporal, daCC, and insular cortices than specific dimensions; spatial overlap in deviations between depression and ADHD groups diminished when controlling for overall psychopathology.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Using deviations from normative models significantly improved prediction of overall psychopathology (correlation with true values: deviations yielded r>raw volume, p<0.05FDR), psychosis-positive symptoms (correlation, RMSE, MAE all better for deviations, p<0.05FDR), and fear (MAE better for deviations, p<0.05FDR) compared to raw cortical volume in out-of-sample testing. Even for dimensions where predictive performance was not above chance levels (externalizing, psychosis-negative, anxious-misery), deviations still showed significantly better performance in some metrics. Overall psychopathology correlated significantly with deviations in vmPFC/mOFC (r=-0.15, p<0.05FDR), inferior temporal (r=-0.15, p<0.05FDR), daCC (r=-0.12, p<0.05FDR), and insular cortices (r=-0.11, p<0.05FDR), indicating greater negative deviations with higher symptom scores. Bootstrapped comparisons revealed that correlations between deviations and overall psychopathology were significantly larger (p<0.01) than those for specific dimensions in vmPFC/mOFC (vs. psychosis-negative and anxious-misery), inferior temporal cortex (vs. psychosis-negative and externalizing), and daCC (vs. psychosis-negative and anxious-misery). In case-control analyses, spatial correlation between Cohen's d maps for depression and ADHD groups was r=0.15 (p=0.002) without controlling for overall psychopathology, but decreased to r=0.08 (p=0.13, Δr=0.07) when controlling for overall psychopathology, suggesting that spatial overlap in group-level deviations was largely explained by overall psychopathology rather than disorder-specific effects.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design limits ability to model intra-individual variability in neurodevelopment over time; focus on T1-weighted cortical features excludes white matter and multimodal information; socioeconomic status and general intelligence confounded prediction models; single-site data limits generalizability to multi-site settings
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: A limitation of this study is the use of cross-sectional data to model neurodevelopment. It is well documented that individual variability in neurodevelopment occurs at both the inter-individual and intra-individual level, and characterizing the factors that explain the latter will be critical for predicting the emergence of psychopathology over time. ... Another limitation is the focus on T1-weighted cortical brain features. ... Here, we focused on cortical volume derived from T1-weighted imaging data owing to the robust relationship with age, which is well suited to normative modeling. Future work that builds multimodal normative models of neurodevelopment may provide additional insights ... Finally, we note that controlling for socioeconomic status and general intelligence in our predictive models resulted in many of our prediction models dropping below significance under our permutation test (see Supplementary Materials), suggesting that these measures confounded our prediction models. ... However, this interpretation remains speculative, since our analysis was restricted to a single site. In order to examine whether the improved predictive performance observed here generalizes to new samples, future work should consider using a normative model trained on one site to understand variance in brain data acquired from a different site.
caa10_key_limitations.location: Parkes2021.pdf.md: Discussion / Limitations, L172-176; Discussion / Conclusions, L179-180

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Used p-factor bifactor model to derive orthogonal psychopathology dimensions (overall psychopathology, anxious-misery, psychosis-positive, psychosis-negative, externalizing, fear) from 117 clinical symptom measures; inverse normal transformation applied to psychopathology dimensions; sensitivity analyses excluded individuals on psychoactive medication (n=142) which revealed additional significant predictions for psychosis-negative and externalizing; alternative parcellation (Lausanne463) yielded consistent results; controlled for multiple nuisance covariates including age, sex, maternal education, T1 QA, T1 SNR, and general intelligence across various sensitivity analyses

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study represents an important application of normative modeling to transdiagnostic psychiatry research, using the p-factor framework to separate disorder-general from disorder-specific biomarkers. The PNC cohort includes 1,271 individuals aged 8-22 years after quality control, with 381 having no clinically significant symptoms. The study design carefully separated the normative reference sample (n=281 healthy) from the testing sample (n=990 including 100 healthy + 890 with psychopathology) to enable true out-of-sample prediction testing. A key innovation is the explicit comparison of normative deviations against raw brain features to demonstrate the added value of normative modeling. The GPR approach captures both nonlinear age effects and heteroscedastic variance, providing z-score deviations that account for both normative variance and predictive uncertainty. The finding that overall psychopathology (p-factor) explains common abnormalities previously attributed to specific disorders challenges traditional case-control approaches and supports transdiagnostic frameworks. Code is available at: https://github.com/lindenmp/normative_neurodev_cs_t1. Data is available through dbGaP: phs000607.v3.p2. The study was conducted on a single scanner without hardware/firmware changes, eliminating site effects as a confound.
